paragraphs: Grocery Outlet is a growth-oriented extreme value retailer of quality, name-brand consumables and fresh products sold primarily through a network of independently operated stores. As of January 3, 2026, we had 570 stores in California, Washington, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Idaho, Nevada, Maryland, Ohio, New Jersey, North Carolina, Georgia, Alabama, Delaware, Kentucky and Virginia. Our headquarters is in Emeryville, California.

Each of our stores offers a fun, treasure hunt shopping experience in an easy-to-navigate, small-box format. An ever-changing assortment of "WOW!" deals, complemented by everyday staple products, generates customer excitement and encourages frequent visits from bargain-minded shoppers. Our flexible buying model allows us to offer quality, name-brand opportunistic products at prices generally 40% to 70% below those of conventional retailers. Our Grocery Outlet stores are primarily run by entrepreneurial independent operators ("IOs") who create a neighborhood feel through personalized customer service and a localized product offering. This differentiated approach has historically driven positive comparable store sales growth.
Our differentiated model for buying and selling delivers a "WOW!" shopping experience, which generates customer excitement, inspires loyalty and supports profitable sales growth:

•How we buy: We source quality, name-brand consumables and fresh products opportunistically through a centralized purchasing team that leverages long-standing and actively managed supplier relationships to acquire merchandise at significant discounts. Our speed and efficiency in responding to supplier needs, combined with our specialized supply chain capabilities and flexible merchandising strategy, enhance our access to discounted products and allow us to turn inventory quickly and profitably. Our buyers proactively source on-trend products based on changing consumer preferences, including a wide selection of Natural, Organic, Specialty or Healthy ("NOSH") products. We also source everyday staple products and have recently introduced our own private label products to complement our opportunistic offerings. Each store offers a curated and ever-changing assortment of items, creating a "buy now" sense of urgency that promotes return visits and fosters customer loyalty.

•How we sell: Our Grocery Outlet stores are primarily independently operated by entrepreneurial IOs, who are small business owners that have a relentless focus on selecting the best products for their communities, providing personalized customer service and driving improved store performance. Unlike a store manager of a traditional retailer, IOs are independent businesses and are responsible for store operations, including ordering, merchandising and managing inventory, marketing locally and directly hiring, training and employing their store workers. IOs initially contribute capital to establish their business and generally share 50% of store-level gross profits with us. These factors both align our interests and incentivize IOs to grow their business profitably to realize financial upside. This combination of local decision-making supported by our purchasing scale and corporate resources results in a "small business at scale" model that we believe is difficult for competitors to replicate.

Our value proposition has broad appeal with bargain-minded customers across a broad range of income levels, demographics and geographies. We believe that our sustained focus on delivering ever-changing "WOW!" deals within a fun, treasure hunt shopping environment has generated strong customer loyalty and brand affinity. We believe that our broad customer appeal supports new store growth opportunities, and we plan to continue to expand our reach to additional customers and geographies.

Our stores generally have performed well across all economic cycles, and for the vast majority of our history, we have had positive comparative sales growth and healthy gross margin rates. Our model also is somewhat insulated from store labor-related variability because IOs directly employ their store workers. The result is a highly scalable business with lower corporate fixed costs, providing further protection in the event of an economic downturn and growth opportunities in a strong economy.

On April 1, 2024, Grocery Outlet Inc., our wholly owned subsidiary, acquired The Bargain Barn, Inc., which does business as United Grocery Outlet ("United Grocery Outlet," or "UGO"), which included 40 stores in six adjacent states we did not operate in as of such date (Tennessee, North Carolina, Georgia, Alabama, Kentucky and Virginia) and a company-operated distribution center. See Note 15 to the consolidated financial statements for additional information.

Throughout this report, the discussion of our business, stores, operations and strategies generally refers to our IO-operated stores. As of January 3, 2026, 41 stores, including 39 United Grocery Outlet stores, were Company-operated stores. Unless otherwise specifically disclosed in this report, the impact of the United Grocery Outlet stores in aggregate was not material to our operations and our consolidated financial statements in fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024.

Our founder, Jim Read, pioneered our opportunistic buying model in 1946 and subsequently developed the IO selling approach, which harnesses individual entrepreneurship and local decision-making to better serve our customers. Underlying this differentiated model was a mission that still guides us today: "Touching Lives for the Better." Since 2006, the third generation of Read family leadership, Eric Lindberg, Jr., Chairman of our Board of Directors (the "Board") and former Chief Executive Officer, has continued to advance this mission.
Grocery Outlet Holding Corp. was incorporated in Delaware on September 11, 2014. Our common stock has traded on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol "GO" since 2019.

We believe that our compelling WOW! shopping experience will continue to drive new and existing customers to shop our stores. Propelled by our strong business fundamentals, we believe we are well-positioned to expand our footprint and grow our customer base. We are executing a long-term growth strategy built on three primary pillars:

•Strengthen our core business model. Our unique buying and selling approach has always been and will continue to be the growth engine of this business. It differentiates us and provides a compelling value proposition to a wide range of customers. We remain focused on deepening our value, strengthening the treasure hunt shopping experience, elevating IO support, and increasing customer awareness, acquisition, and retention. We continually seek to strengthen supplier relationships and further develop opportunistic purchasing with new processes and investments.

•Evolve our business. We are focused on advancing our model through optimizing our assortment and digitizing our business with more integrated end-to-end technology. We also continue to implement operational initiatives to support IOs in enhancing the customer experience.

paragraphs: The following risk factors are important to understanding various statements in this Form 10-K or elsewhere. The factors described below, individually or in the aggregate, could materially adversely affect our business, business prospects, financial condition, operating results, cash flows and stock price, and may cause actual results, performance or achievements in future periods to differ materially from those assumed, projected or contemplated. Moreover, we operate in a very competitive and rapidly changing environment, and new risks emerge from time to time.
The following is a summary of the principal risks that could adversely affect our business, operations and financial results:
•failure of suppliers to consistently supply us with opportunistic products at attractive pricing, which is generally not in our control;
•inability to successfully identify trends and maintain an appropriate level of opportunistic products or general inventory;
•failure to maintain or increase comparable store sales;
•any significant disruption to our distribution and transportation network, the operations, technology and capacity of our distribution centers and our timely receipt of inventory;

paragraphs: Key financial and operating performance results for our fiscal 2025 compared to our fiscal 2024 were as follows:

•Net sales increased by 7.3% to $4.69 billion for fiscal 2025 from $4.37 billion for fiscal 2024. Fiscal 2025 contained one additional week ("53rd week") as compared to fiscal 2024. The 53rd week included $82.4 million in net sales.
•Comparable store sales increased by 0.5% in fiscal 2025 on a 52-week basis, driven by a 1.6% increase in the number of transactions partially offset by a 1.1% decrease in average transaction size.
•Gross margin increased by 10 basis points to 30.3%, compared to gross margin of 30.2% for fiscal 2024.
•We opened 42 new stores and closed five, ending fiscal 2025 with 570 stores in 16 states.
•SG&A increased by 8.5% to $1.33 billion, or 28.4% of net sales.

•Operating loss was $221.7 million, which included $113.8 million in impairment of long-lived assets, $45.9 million in charges related to the Restructuring Plan and $149.0 million in non-cash charges related to the impairment of goodwill. Impairment of long-lived assets related to certain underperforming stores, substantially all of which we subsequently determined to close as part of the Optimization Plan. See Note 5 and Note 16 to the consolidated financial statements for additional information.
•Net loss was $224.9 million, or $(2.30) per diluted share for fiscal 2025, compared to net income of $39.5 million, or $0.40 per diluted share, for fiscal 2024.

•Adjusted net income(1) decreased by 1.5% to $75.2 million, or $0.76 diluted adjusted earnings per share(1), compared to $76.3 million, or $0.77 diluted adjusted earnings per share(1), for fiscal 2024.
•Adjusted EBITDA(1) was $254.3 million in fiscal 2025 compared to $236.8 million in fiscal 2024.

(1)Adjusted net income, diluted adjusted earnings per share and adjusted EBITDA are non-GAAP financial measures, which exclude the impact of certain special items. Please note that our non-GAAP financial measures should be considered as a supplement to, and not as a substitute for, or superior to, financial measures calculated in accordance with GAAP. See the "Operating Metrics and Non-GAAP Financial Measures" section below for additional information about these items, including their definitions, how the non-GAAP financial measures provide useful information to investors and how management utilizes them, and reconciliations of the non-GAAP financial measures and the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures.

paragraphs: Grocery Outlet 是一家以成長為導向的極端價值零售業者，銷售高品質、知名品牌的消耗性商品與新鮮產品，主要透過一張由獨立經營商店組成的網路進行銷售。截至 2026 年 1 月 3 日，我們在加州、華盛頓州、俄勒岡州、賓州、田納西州、愛達荷州、內華達州、馬裏蘭州、俄亥俄州、新澤西州、北卡羅來納州、喬治亞州、阿拉巴馬州、特拉華州、肯塔基州與維吉尼亞州共有 570 家商店。我們的總部位於加州的埃默裏維爾市。

我們每一家商店都提供一個有趣、尋寶般的購物體驗，透過一個容易導航的小型商店格式。不斷變化的 "WOW!" 特價商品，搭配日常必需品，會讓顧客感到興奮，並鼓勵追求折扣商品的顧客頻繁造訪。我們靈活的採購模式讓我們能以通常比傳統零售商低 40% 到 70% 的價格，提供高品質、知名品牌的機會性商品。我們的 Grocery Outlet 商店主要由創業型獨立經營者（"IOs"）經營，他們透過個性化的顧客服務與當地化商品選擇，營造出社區感。這種差異化的模式歷來推動了正向的同店銷售額成長。
我們差異化的採購與銷售模式，提供了 "WOW!" 的購物體驗，這會讓顧客感到興奮，激勵忠誠度，並支持獲利性的銷售成長：

•我們如何採購：我們透過一個中央採購團隊，以機會性的方式採購高品質、知名品牌的消耗性商品與新鮮產品。該團隊利用長期且積極管理的供應商關係，以獲得顯著折扣的商品。我們對供應商需求的快速與高效回應，結合我們專業的供應鏈能力與靈活的商品策略，增強我們取得折扣商品的機會，並讓我們能快速且獲利地轉換存貨。我們的採購者會根據消費者的變動偏好，主動尋找時尚商品，包括廣泛的自然、有機、專門或健康（"NOSH"）商品。我們也採購日常必需品，並最近推出了自有品牌商品，以補充我們的機會性商品。每一家商店都提供一個精心策劃且不斷變化的商品組合，創造出 "現在就買" 的緊迫感，促進顧客回訪並培養忠誠度。

•我們如何銷售：我們的 Grocery Outlet 商店主要由創業型 IOs 獨立經營，他們是小型企業所有者，對選擇最適合他們社區的商品、提供個性化的顧客服務以及提升商店表現有極強的專注。與傳統零售商的商店經理不同，IOs 是獨立企業，並負責商店的營運，包括訂購、商品陳列與管理存貨、當地行銷，以及直接僱用、培訓與僱用商店員工。IOs 初期會投入資金來建立他們的業務，並通常與我們共享商店層級的毛利收入的 50%。這些因素同時使我們的利潤與 IOs 的利潤產生一致性，並激勵 IOs 以獲利的方式成長他們的業務，以實現財務上的回報。這種由我們採購規模與公司資源支持的本地決策，形成了我們所稱的 "規模化的中小企業" 模式，我們認為這對競爭對手來說很難複製。
我們的價值主張對追求折扣商品的顧客有廣泛的吸引力，這些顧客來自不同收入層級、人口統計與地理區域。我們相信，我們持續專注於在一個有趣、尋寶般的購物環境中提供不斷變化的 "WOW!" 特價商品，已經產生了強大的顧客忠誠度與品牌親近感。我們相信，我們廣泛的顧客吸引力支持了新店成長的機會，我們計畫繼續擴展我們的觸及範圍至更多的顧客與地理區域。
我們的商店在所有經濟週期中通常表現良好，而且在我們的大部分歷史中，我們都擁有正向的同店銷售成長與健康的毛利率。我們的模式也較不受商店勞動相關變動的影響，因為 IOs 直接僱用他們的商店員工。結果是一個高度可擴展的業務，擁有較低的公司固定成本，這在經濟衰退時提供了進一步的保護，並在經濟強勁時提供了成長機會。

2024 年 4 月 1 日，我們的全資子公司 Grocery Outlet Inc. 收購了 The Bargain Barn, Inc.，該公司以 United Grocery Outlet（"United Grocery Outlet" 或 "UGO"）為商號，包括在該日期我們未經營的六個相鄰州的 40 家商店（田納西州、北卡羅來納州、喬治亞州、阿拉巴馬州、肯塔基州與維吉尼亞州）以及一個公司經營的配送中心。請參閱財務報表附註 15 獲取更多資訊。
本報告中，對於我們業務、門市、營運與策略的討論，通常是指我們IO經營的門市。截至2026年1月3日，共有41間門市，包括39間United Grocery Outlet門市，為本公司經營的門市。除非本報告另有明確說明，否則United Grocery Outlet門市對我們營運及2025財年與2024財年合併財務報表的影響並非重大。
我們創辦人Jim Read於1946年開創了我們的機會性採購模式，並隨後發展出IO銷售方式，此方式透過個人創業精神與地方決策，以更好地服務我們的客戶。此區別化模式背後的使命至今仍引導著我們："Touching Lives for the Better." 自2006年起，Read家族第三代領導者Eric Lindberg, Jr.，本公司董事會（"董事會"）主席及前首席執行官，持續推動此使命。
Grocery Outlet Holding Corp.於2014年9月11日在德拉瓦州註冊成立。我們的普通股自2019年起在納斯達克全球選択市場（Nasdaq Global Select Market）以符號"GO"交易。
我們相信，我們令人驚嘆的WOW! 購物體驗將持續吸引新舊客戶來光顧我們的門市。在強勁的業務基礎之上，我們相信我們已處於良好的位置，以擴大我們的業務版圖並增長客戶羣。我們正在執行一項長期成長策略，其基礎為三個主要支柱：
•強化我們的核心業務模式。我們獨特的採購與銷售方式始終是並將持續是此業務的成長引擎。此方式使我們與其他競爭者區隔，並為廣泛的客戶羣提供有吸引力的價值主張。我們持續專注於深化我們的價值，強化寶藏尋找購物體驗，提升IO支援，並增加客戶認知、獲取與留存。我們持續尋求強化供應商關係，並透過新流程與投資進一步發展機會性採購。
•進化我們的業務。我們專注於透過優化商品種類與以更整合的端到端科技數位化業務來提升我們的模式。我們也持續執行運營方案，以支援IO提升客戶體驗。

paragraphs: 本公司財務與營運績效表現，財務年度2025年與財務年度2024年比較如下：
•淨銷售額較財務年度2024年的43.7億美元增加7.3%至財務年度2025年的46.9億美元。財務年度2025年包含多出的一週（"53週"），與財務年度2024年相比。53週包含淨銷售額82.4百萬美元。
•在52週基礎下，財務年度2025年的同店銷售額成長0.5%，主要因交易筆數增加1.6%，部分抵銷平均交易金額減少1.1%的影響。
•毛利率提高10個基點至30.3%，與財務年度2024年的30.2%毛利率相比。
•財務年度2025年，本公司開設42家新店並關閉5家，截至財務年度2025年結束時，總計在16州擁有570家門市。
•銷售及一般行政費用增加8.5%至13.3億美元，或佔淨銷售額的28.4%。
•營運虧損為221.7百萬美元，包含113.8百萬美元長期資產減損、45.9百萬美元與重整計畫相關費用，以及149.0百萬美元與商譽減損相關的非現金費用。長期資產減損與部分表現不佳門市有關，本公司隨後決定將這些門市關閉作為優化計畫的一部分。有關更多資訊，請參閱財務報表附註第5項及第16項。
•淨虧損為224.9百萬美元，或每股稀釋後虧損2.30美元，與財務年度2024年的淨利潤39.5百萬美元，或每股稀釋後收益0.40美元相比。
•調整後淨收入(1) 下降 1.5% 至 75.2 百萬美元，或 0.76 稀釋調整後每股盈餘(1)，較財務 2024 年的 76.3 百萬美元，或 0.77 稀釋調整後每股盈餘(1) 減少。
•調整後營業現金流(1) 在財務年度 2025 年為 254.3 百萬美元，較財務年度 2024 年的 236.8 百萬美元

(1)調整後淨收入、稀釋調整後每股盈餘及調整後營業現金流為非 GAAP 會計財務指標，其排除某些特殊項目之影響。請注意，我們的非 GAAP 財務指標應視為對 GAAP 財務指標的補充，而非替代或更優於 GAAP 財務指標。請參閱下方「營運指標與非 GAAP 財務指標」部分，以取得這些項目之更多資訊，包括其定義、非 GAAP 財務指標對投資者之資訊價值，以及管理階層如何運用這些指標，以及非 GAAP 財務指標與最直接可比較之 GAAP 財務指標之調和資料

我們依賴供應商持續提供具競爭優勢的產品並以有吸引力的價格供應，這通常不在我們的控制範圍內。
我們可能無法成功識別趨勢以符合消費者需求，並維持適當的具競爭優勢產品或一般存貨水準。
若我們無法在長遠內持續實現可比的店面成長，將可能對我們的獲利能力和表現造成重大不利影響。
我們新開設的店面可能在短時間內對我們的財務結果產生負面影響，且可能無法在及時或任何情況下達到與我們較成熟店面一致的銷售與營運水準。

paragraphs: 下列風險因素對理解本 Form 10-K 或其他地方的各項陳述具有重要意義。下列所述因素，單獨或合計，可能會重大且負面影響本公司業務、業務前景、財務狀況、營運結果、現金流及股票價格，並可能使未來期間的實際結果、表現或成就與假設、預測或預期的情況有重大差異。此外，本公司營運環境極具競爭且快速變動，並時常出現新的風險。
